summary: Feed s148_double is degraded: 24.66 Gbps microburst exceeds 10 Gbps NDR port (247% capacity) causing egress queue overflow and 2.5% TCP packet drops (200/8061), degrading NDR detection coverage.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker forwards line-rate microbursts without load balancing or shaping: 24.66 Gbps peak in 1ms interval vs 10 Gbps NDR tool port (147% over capacity, 247% of capacity total). Egress buffer overflows at broker tool port.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR port drops traffic during bursts, misses packets/flows, TCP reassembly fails and detections are missed; burst loss creates blind spots for threat detection.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute microbursts across 3x10G NDR ports (30G aggregate) via 5-tuple load balancing so no single 10G port exceeds capacity; eliminates 24.66 Gbps overload and prevents burst drops while preserving full payload for NDR.

findings.root_cause: 2.5% TCP sequence gaps (200 of 8061 packets) caused by same tool-port overload: broker egress queue drops packets when 24.66 Gbps burst exceeds 10 Gbps port, not random link errors.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR requires full payload and both directions; missing segments break stream reassembly, file extraction and IDS signatures fail, causing false negatives and incomplete flow records.

recommended_fix.why: Same overload root cause as tool_overload; load balancing bursts across multiple tool ports removes egress drops and restores complete TCP streams without filtering or slicing which would hurt NDR payload needs.
